content.theory:
Flexbox is the modern way to arrange items in a row or column — and center them without hacks.

### Make a container flex
```css
.container {
  display: flex;
}
```
Its children become **flex items** laid out in a row by default.

### Main axis & direction
```css
.flex-row { display: flex; flex-direction: row; }        /* left → right */
.flex-col { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }     /* top → bottom */
```

### Justify & align
- `justify-content` → positions items along the **main axis**
- `align-items` → positions items along the **cross axis**

```css
.container {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: center;   /* center horizontally (row) */
  align-items: center;       /* center vertically (row) */
}
```
That single snippet is the classic "perfectly center a box" recipe.

### Spacing options
```css
justify-content: flex-start;    /* default, left */
justify-content: center;        /* grouped center */
justify-content: space-between; /* first & last at edges, equal gaps */
justify-content: space-around;  /* equal space around each */
justify-content: space-evenly;  /* fully even gaps */
```

### Grow to fill
```css
.item { flex: 1; }   /* each item takes equal share */
```

### Gap (modern, simple)
```css
.container { display: flex; gap: 16px; }
```
`gap` adds spacing between items without fiddly margins.

exercise.instruction: Style .row so its three .box children sit in a row, evenly spaced with space-between, and vertically centered. Add a 12px gap.
hints: Hint 1: Set display: flex; to enable flexbox.
Hint 2: Use justify-content: space-between; to spread the boxes out.
Hint 3: Add align-items: center; and gap: 12px;.

quiz.question: Which property centers items along the cross axis?
Which value spreads items to the edges with equal gaps?
